summary: Shingled 20.1 m rear range light on Glover's Shore Road, Summerside PEI, lit 1895 to line up with the railway-wharf front light; enclosed 1904; kept 1912-36 by Fred Muttart.

structures.note: Built as an open-frame pyramidal tower, 17 m (56 ft) high (LF). Enclosed 1904; moved 1913 or 1914; height raised 1916. Shingled, with a red stripe (PEILS; CCG).
Front range light on the railway wharf replaced by a metal (skeleton) tower with a light in 1961 (Register; LF). Not this record's structure; recorded as the pair's partner.

staffing.note: Lighthouse Friends: automated in 1952 under Harry Heckbert. PEI Lighthouse Society data sheet: 'De-staffed in 1961'. The two dates disagree.

access.note: Grounds and tower closed (LF). Visible from Glover's Shore Road (PEILS directions).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (federal). Heritage Guide: owned by the Government of Canada. The City of Summerside petitioned for ownership under the Parks Canada heritage lighthouse programme (LF).

events.note: Rear range tower built at a cost of $225 by Milton Walsh on the Stavert farm (LF; PEILS).
Put in operation on 5 Sept 1895 (LF; PEILS). The 1903 keeper table dates a keeper's appointment to 8 Sept 1895 (read by position).
Tower enclosed and painted white (LF; Register).
PEI Lighthouse Society: moved 50 feet south in 1913. Lighthouse Friends: new site bought and tower relocated in 1914 for $587.37. The dates disagree.
Addition costing $212.63 raised the height of the light (LF; Department report for 1915-16).
Harry H. Heckbert took charge after Fred Muttart was dismissed (LF).
Automated, per Lighthouse Friends. The PEI Lighthouse Society says de-staffed in 1961.
Front range tower replaced by a metal tower with a light (Register; LF). PEILS gives de-staffing of the back light in 1961.
Recognized by the City of Summerside as a registered historic place on 4 Dec 2007 (Canadian Register 10116; LF).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Canadian Register gives 'Built 1895-1904': 1895 is the construction and first light; 1904 is the enclosure of the tower. Both are consistent with the sources.
Automation in 1952 (LF) and de-staffing in 1961 (PEILS) are not reconciled by the sources. Both are given in the story.
Lighthouse Friends says the large ferry steamers ran between Summerside and New Brunswick; the PEI Lighthouse Society says Nova Scotia. The story gives both and does not choose.

PEILS says the range was moved 50 feet south in 1913; Lighthouse Friends says the site was bought and the tower relocated in 1914 for $587.37. The 1913 move and the 1914 purchase are both in the story.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-27. Changed: 'Prince County' removed (no cited source gives it; the Heritage Guide and PEILS say Summerside, Prince Edward Island); the ferry route is now given as disputed (LF: New Brunswick; PEILS: Nova Scotia) rather than attributed to the Register, which does not mention the ferries' route; 'The harbour needed help' removed as editorial; the 1904 keeper list entry now says only that 'Stavart, Geo' is in the list (the station beside the name is not clear in the OCR, so the story does not place him at the rear light); 'a 50 feet (15 m)' reversed to metres first; the process caveat about the 1903 table read by position moved out of the prose. The 1903 keeper-table row ('Summerside Harbour Range Back Light Sept, 8, 1895', printed p. 220) is read from OCR row order and not checked against the page image; the 1914 Muttart row is a labelled table ('Name of Station' / 'Name of Lightkeeper') at printed p. 62, confirmed by corpus page; the 1916 addition row ('Summerside - Addition to back range light tower ... 212 63') is at printed p. 49, confirmed. The 1904 'Stavart, Geo' line is in an alphabetical name list at printed p. 164 (confirmed by corpus page); its station is not read. CCG list no. 1022 (rear range) matches the story: fixed green, 24.8 m, 16 nm, 'White pyramid tower with red upper portion and red vertical stripe'. Nominal range disagrees: PEILS 18 nm, CCG 16 nm (story uses CCG). PEILS GPS coordinates (46 23 14.4 N, 63 47 21.2 W) differ from the CCG position (46 23 28.7 N, 63 46 17.2 W), which the record uses; left unchanged. Automation 1952 (LF) and de-staffing 1961 (PEILS) are both in the story. Ferguson is placed at the back light by PEILS and at the front light by LF; the roster keeps the PEILS line and the story gives both. Front and back range names: LF 'Summerside Range Rear'; the Register and PEILS 'Back Range Light'; same light. No storms, wrecks or rescues tied to this light were found in the Marine reports read; no newspaper search was run for this station. The Canadian Register page (historicplaces.ca id 10116) returned only a fragment; the Heritage Guide copy of the register text was quoted. Post-1960 keeper: Ferguson (service to 1961) is named only as PEILS and LF print him, with no personal detail.
